extensions.title: Windows mandatory file locking during update, rollback and uninstall
extensions.question: POSIX allows unlinking and replacing a file another process holds open; Windows takes a mandatory lock and the same operation fails with a sharing violation. Target: hold an open handle on each file the lifecycle commands must replace (a loaded hook script, an active log, a running interpreter's own module) and assert the command either completes via a replace-on-reboot / rename-then-write strategy or fails with a message naming the locking process - never a partial replacement. Which lifecycle step leaves the install half-updated when a handle is held?
extensions.answer: naive in-place sequential replace during update: unlocked plugin.json / skills / rules become 2.0.0, then the held hooks/on_load.py raises WinError 32 and stays 1.0.0 — mixed tree, which is a P0 even if the command later exits non-zero. The same sequential unlink during uninstall half-removes the tree. Locked-aware update/rollback/uninstall preflight and refuse, naming pid= and the locking process, leaving the inventory byte-identical.

scope.proof_surface: Disposable plugin tree under a WinLockFS overlay that raises WinError 32 on overwrite/unlink of held paths. Scoped to file LOCKING; MSYS argument rewriting is TST-0190 and is not duplicated.
does_not_claim: A native Windows handle table was enumerated on this Linux host.
platform/plugin CLI is present on this worktree; the SUT is the locked-aware lifecycle kernel plus the naive sequential control.
